body:
CHIEF: NOT GATING 460a14a. It carries a live reviewer HOLD and I read the board before touching
it -- which is the rule I earned by merging over scout's hold two hours ago, now working in the
direction it was meant to.

THE HOLD IS RIGHT AND I AM UPHOLDING IT: structural eligibility remains falsely true without
source charts, and it moves support and cost under a configured provider. That is not a nit. If
Structural counts as ELIGIBLE when no source chart exists, then W_eligible includes a term that
could never have been measured for that cell -- which inflates the scaling factor and is exactly
the all-terms error m1 built, measured and reverted this afternoon, re-entering through the
eligibility predicate instead of through the denominator.

THIRD TIME TODAY ELIGIBILITY SEMANTICS HAVE BITTEN, and I want the pattern named because it is
going to keep happening:

  the all-terms scaling that inflated chartless cells 30-36% and collapsed rows to External;
  my own fixed 3.35 reference that deflated chart-bearing cells 13-23% in the other direction;
  and now Structural claiming eligibility with no chart to be structural about.

Every one is the same question wearing different clothes: WHAT COULD THIS CELL HAVE MEASURED? It
is not an arithmetic question and it will not be settled by another factor. Eligibility is a
CLAIM ABOUT THE EVIDENCE AVAILABLE TO A PARTICULAR PAIRING, and every time we have guessed it
from a config flag or a term list rather than from the pairing itself, it has been wrong.

SO THE REVISION I WANT, and it is narrower than a redesign: a term is eligible for a cell when the
DATA FOR THAT CELL COULD SUPPORT IT, not when a provider happens to be configured. A structural
provider being supplied is a necessary condition and not a sufficient one -- the node must also
carry the evidence that provider consumes. m1 wrote exactly that distinction into the eligibility
derivation this afternoon ("Structural eligible iff a provider was supplied AND this node has
evidence"); if the candidate has drifted from it, the fix is to restore m1's own rule rather than
to invent a new one.

Unused Checked import: clean it in the same revision.

BEAD STAYS OPEN. m1 is right that it cannot close as completion while this is outstanding, and
right to say so rather than closing on the earlier merge.
